cosy-lesson.title: Why Grandparents Matter More Than Ever for Children's Mental Health

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Extended family – family members beyond parents and children, such as grandparents, aunts, and uncles.

p.em: Example: In some cultures, the extended family plays a big role in raising children.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mental health – a person's emotional and psychological well-being.

p.em: Example: Good mental health helps people cope with stress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Emotional resilience – the ability to recover from difficulties and challenges.

p.em: Example: Sports can help children develop emotional resilience.

cosy-blockquote.p: Achievement pressure – stress caused by expectations to succeed.

p.em: Example: Many teenagers experience achievement pressure at school.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sense of purpose – a feeling that your life has meaning and direction.

p.em: Example: Volunteering gave her a stronger sense of purpose.

cosy-blockquote.p: Empathy ≠ Apathy – the ability to understand other's feelings ≠ a lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.

p.em: Example: Hearing people's thoughts taught him true empathy, replacing his lifelong cold apathy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Encouragement – support that gives someone confidence or hope.

p.em: Example: A few words of encouragement can make a big difference.

cosy-blockquote.p: Criticism – expressing disapproval or pointing out mistakes.

p.em: Example: Constant criticism can damage a child's confidence.

cosy-blockquote.p: Growth mindset – the belief that abilities can improve through effort and learning.

p.em: Example: A growth mindset helps people learn from failures.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cope with – to deal successfully with a difficult situation.

p.em: Example: Children need support to cope with disappointment.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, why is regular contact with the extended family more vital for children's mental wellness today?
★ How close was your relationship with your grandparents when you were growing up?

What evidence is presented in the study to show that children who have close grandparental bonds possess superior mental health?
★ Do you think children today spend enough face-to-face time with their extended family?

According to the researchers, why does a strong bond with older relatives improve emotional resilience better than external rewards?
★ Who in your family did you go to for emotional comfort when you were a child?

What data in the article explains how high achievement pressure at school contributes to child anxiety?
★ How often did your family host large multi-generational gatherings?

Based on the study, how does having a strong sense of purpose protect a child's psychological development?
★ Do you believe that family support is the best medicine for youth mental health?

How does the psychologist differentiate between genuine empathy ≠ apathy when examining parent-child interactions?
★ What is a skill or hobby you learned directly from an older relative?

According to the article, why does small verbal encouragement serve as "molecules of emotional health"?
★ How do you personally handle stress, and did your family teach you this?

Based on the research findings, why does constant criticism reduce motivation instead of improving behavior?
★ Do you think modern social media is making teenagers lonelier than past generations?

What parameters in the study support praising effort to build a child's growth mindset?
★ What family tradition do you hope to keep alive in your own future family?

According to the paper, what strategies help children cope with disappointment and cognitive fatigue?
★ Do you think older relatives benefit mentally from spending time with young kids?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this hypothesis, communities will design physical housing to merge senior homes with child care to boost extended family support.
★ Would you move closer to your family if it meant better mental health for your kids?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, we will prove that mental health decay is directly correlated with lack of intergenerational stories.
★ Do you think the concept of the extended family is disappearing in western countries?

Imagine future research shows that emotional resilience is physically transferred via play, we will build play-labs for elders and children.
★ Should companies offer paid leave for grandparents to help care for newborn babies?

If future research proves this discovery beyond doubt, schools will eliminate traditional grades to protect children from achievement pressure.
★ Do you think our mental health is shaped more by our genes or our childhood environment?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, every child's curriculum will focus on developing a biological sense of purpose rather than standardized testing.
★ Would you trust an online support group more than your own family in a crisis?

Imagine future research proves that empathy ≠ apathy pathways are permanently damaged by social media use, smartphones will be banned for minors.
★ How can communities help elderly people who have no grandchildren stay socially active?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, a daily dose of positive encouragement will be prescribed by pediatricians over pharmacological medication.
★ Do you think future schools will have built-in community centers for elders?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, we will verify that unnecessary parental criticism causes permanent neural damage to child motivation networks.
★ What is the most important lesson about mental resilience you have learned in life?

Imagine future research proves that a growth mindset can be structurally activated by grandparent interactions, families will co-habit to protect intelligence.
★ Do you believe that strong family roots make people more independent as adults?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, child psychology will build specialized therapy zones to help children cope with disappointment using ancestor oral histories.
★ How do you think your own mental health has been influenced by your ancestors' stories?

ul.li: Incorrect: My grandparents live here since 20 years → Correct: My grandparents have lived here for 20 years ((Present Perfect + for/since))
Incorrect: I used to visiting them every summer → Correct: I used to visit them every summer ((Used to + infinitive))
Incorrect: It is a very important news → Correct: It is very important news ((Uncountable news))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
Incorrect: It is depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Verb vs Adjective))
